explanation.definitionFit: A parent's sister is a female family member, so she is one kind of relative.

clue.text: University professor laid up - poor soul's covered in lumps

blocks.note: U is the standard abbreviation for university

the four letters of soul rearranged

explanation.surface: A bedridden academic is so ill that his skin has broken out in bumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A nodule is a small swelling or knot, so something nodulous has many of these bumps on it.

clue.text: Leader absolutely raised journalist's plight

explanation.surface: Someone at the top has publicised the sorry situation of a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader absolutely' reads as a ruler who governs absolutely, i.e. with unlimited power; only ED is raised, and SPOT follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant holds absolute power over a country, so he leads with no limits whatever.

clue.text: Buyout affected Mile End - you can see what's around here

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder
the closing letter of Mile

explanation.surface: A takeover has changed an East London district so much that its sights are now on show.
explanation.walkthrough: Mile End is a real area of East London, but here it simply means the end of the word Mile.
explanation.definitionFit: The video-sharing website shows clips of almost everything happening in the world, so viewers watch what is going on there.

clue.text: Others in old accommodation

explanation.walkthrough: 'Old accommodation' means housing for elderly people, not housing that is itself old.

clue.text: Almost immediately arrests one without stress

explanation.definitionFit: Immaculate means spotless or without a single blemish, so free of any dirt or stain.

clue.text: Wrinkly's wig gets tousled on occasion

blocks.note: rug is slang for a toupee
the second, fourth and sixth letters of tousled

explanation.surface: An old person's hairpiece sometimes ends up in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrinkly' looks like a noun for an old person, but it is the adjective; 'tousled' is not an anagram signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugose is a botanical and zoological term for a surface that is ridged, creased or corrugated.

clue.text: Sign initially the union may fold

the first letters of these three words

explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy the omentum is a double layer of peritoneum hanging from the stomach, a fold of membrane.

clue.text: Disreputable female prepared to entertain a more disreputable man?

blocks.note: set means ready or prepared
a jibe at Donald Trump, then US president, as a man of worse repute still

explanation.surface: A woman of loose morals is ready to welcome a man even worse than herself.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second part is a topical joke rather than a dictionary synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Strumpet is an old-fashioned insult for a promiscuous woman or prostitute.

clue.text: Friendly native, Harry, not retiring

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the words run backwards

blocks.note: to harry someone is to nag them, followed by not

explanation.surface: A sociable local called Harry who is anything but shy.
explanation.walkthrough: Tonga is known as the Friendly Islands, the name Captain Cook gave it, so a Friendly native is one of its people.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga's nickname is the Friendly Islands, so someone born there is literally a native of the Friendlies.

clue.text: Shepherd's pie at last - I'm surprised in a way

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word before it
in places one piece within the next

blocks.note: the closing letter of pie
ST, street, is a way

explanation.surface: A shepherd's pie finally arrives, and someone is quite astonished by it.
explanation.walkthrough: Shepherd's pie is a British dish of minced lamb topped with mashed potato; here 'Shepherd' is a verb, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To shepherd people is to guide or accompany them, which is what an escort does.

clue.text: Site of famous mission to moon - NASA not bothered about name

indicators.note: something bothered is agitated and stirred up, so these letters are jumbled
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: the seven letters of these two words rearranged
N is the abbreviation for name
Io is one of Jupiter's moons

explanation.surface: A space agency unfazed about naming the place for a celebrated lunar mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mission to moon' suggests space travel, but the mission is the Alamo, a Spanish mission church; 'moon' is Io, which follows the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alamo, the old Spanish mission besieged in 1836, stands in this Texas city.

clue.text: Reading supporters barrack new left-back (United's replacement for Ashley originally)

originally points to how the word begins, its opening letter

Tyler Blackett, a left-back who joined Reading from Manchester United, clipped to his first five letters
U is the standard abbreviation for United
the first letter of Ashley, the one that is replaced

explanation.surface: Fans of Reading FC jeer their latest full-back signing, who came in to replace an England defender.
explanation.walkthrough: Uncertain parse: the topical football reference is unclear. Reading FC's Tyler Blackett is the likeliest left-back; swapping U for A in BLACK and rearranging gives the remaining letters. 'Reading' looks like the club but means literature.
explanation.definitionFit: A group that meets to discuss books encourages and sustains the habit of literature, so its members back the act of perusing novels.

clue.text: 'Totnes Tories not all there' - wise guy!

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: A sarcastic jibe at the Conservatives of Totnes, a Devon town, as half-witted, aimed at some smart alec.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer, Nestor is the aged king of Pylos famed for sage advice, so his name means a wise old counsellor.

clue.text: Paul Bunyan maybe upriver hacking at tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up the river means reading its name from the bottom upwards
hacking chops something about, so these letters are cut up and rearranged

blocks.note: the Po, Italy's longest river, turned upwards
the six letters of these two words rearranged

explanation.surface: The legendary American lumberjack, perhaps, travelling up a river and chopping at a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: Paul Bunyan, a giant lumberjack of American folklore, is also the title of Benjamin Britten's first work for the stage, with words by W. H. Auden.
explanation.definitionFit: Britten and Auden called their Paul Bunyan a choral operetta, a light musical stage work, so it is an example.

clue.text: Bed American woman

blocks.note: a berth is a bunk or bed on a ship or train
A is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A lady from the United States who is sleeping.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertha is a female first name, so it stands for an example of a lady.

clue.text: Slip stops easy goal - he may retreat into his shell

definitions.text: he may retreat into his shell

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to fill it, so one word plugs the inside of the other

blocks.note: a tap-in is a goal from very close range
to slip is to make a mistake, to err

explanation.definitionFit: This freshwater turtle pulls its head and legs into its hard carapace when threatened.

clue.text: Staff split over threat to trespassers

blocks.note: to man something is to staff it
to split is to part, here turned over

explanation.surface: Employees fall out over a warning sign aimed at intruders.
explanation.definitionFit: A trap set on private land to catch intruders is a danger that menaces anyone straying onto the property.

clue.text: Here with shooter (not for public consumption)

blocks.note: in means at home, here
a camera shoots pictures, not bullets

explanation.surface: A photographer is present at a private occasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shooter' suggests a gun, but it is the camera.
explanation.definitionFit: A court case heard behind closed doors, privately in a judge's room, is kept secret from the audience.

clue.text: Better though not good - he's in no great hurry

explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as superior; it is one who bets.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who strolls at a leisurely pace walks slowly and is never rushing anywhere.

clue.text: Oberon's enchanted island

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram fodder

explanation.walkthrough: The enchanted island suggests Prospero's in The Tempest, but 'enchanted' is the anagram signal.

clue.text: Support about to vanish for Hollywood activity

clue.text: Spirited females dancing and singing at opening across road

the first letter of singing
